changes.description: Add dependencies @opentelemetry/api, @opentelemetry/sdk-node, @opentelemetry/instrumentation-http and @fastify/otel (latest stable at install time, caret ranges). Add devDependencies @opentelemetry/sdk-trace-base and @opentelemetry/sdk-metrics for in-memory exporters in tests. Change only the dev and start scripts to preload the bootstrap: 'tsx watch --import ./src/instrument.ts src/index.ts' and 'tsx --import ./src/instrument.ts src/index.ts'. If tsx ordering prevents the preload running first, fall back to 'node --import tsx --import ./src/instrument.ts'. typecheck and test scripts are unchanged.
Regenerated by npm install at the repo root to pin the new OpenTelemetry packages. Not hand-edited. Run npm audit and review for high or critical findings.

Telemetry logic with no import of fastify or node:http. resolveTelemetryConfig(env) enables telemetry only when OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, _TRACES_ENDPOINT or _METRICS_ENDPOINT is set and OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is not true; each endpoint must be https, or http on localhost/127.0.0.1/[::1]; invalid endpoints fail closed (telemetry off, one warning that never contains the URL or header values). service.name comes from OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, default 'warehouse-server'. initTelemetry(env, overrides) builds a NodeSDK with HttpInstrumentation (default attributes only, no hooks adding headers or bodies) and @fastify/otel with registerOnInitialization true, lets the SDK pick exporters, protocol, headers, sampler and timeouts from OTEL_* variables, is idempotent, and catches start failures so the server still starts. shutdownTelemetry(timeoutMs = 5000) races sdk.shutdown against a cleared or unref'd timer and swallows errors. Overrides allow in-memory span processors and metric reader for tests.

Preload entry used by --import. Imports initTelemetry from ./telemetry.js and calls it. Registers ESM loader hooks (for example @opentelemetry/instrumentation/hook.mjs via node:module register) only when resolveTelemetryConfig says enabled and only if the installed instrumentation requires it for the node:http built-in. No other logic. Does nothing when telemetry is off.

Import shutdownTelemetry from ./telemetry.js (do not import instrument.ts). After app.listen and the existing console.log, register SIGINT and SIGTERM handlers guarded by a shuttingDown flag that await app.close(), await shutdownTelemetry(), then process.exit(0). Routes, binding to 127.0.0.1 and logging are unchanged.

Contingent, expected no change. Only if the 4xx component test shows @fastify/otel marks handled 4xx errors (HttpError, DuplicateVinError, 404) as ERROR, adjust the error handler branches below 500 (or instrumentation options if available) so the active span is not left in error status, using @opentelemetry/api. Response bodies and status codes stay identical.

node:test suite. Unit: resolveTelemetryConfig for no endpoint, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED, local http allowed, remote http rejected, https allowed, reason text never contains the URL, service.name default and override, traces-only and metrics-only endpoint vars. Component: default-off initTelemetry returns undefined with no output. Component: initTelemetry with in-memory span processor and metric reader overrides before buildApp, then app.inject for GET list (route, method, 200, service.name), GET 404 (no ERROR span), POST with VIN body and GET with query string (no VIN, body or query value in span attributes), shutdown flush and metrics data point. Providers are disabled in teardown for isolation. No network.

Spawns real server processes through the same --import ./src/instrument.ts command shape as npm start, with a loopback-only fake OTLP collector (node:http) in the test process, free ports and a temp WAREHOUSE_DATA_DIR. Cases: default off (200, no telemetry output); enabled with http/json (trace with method, route, status, service.name and an HTTP server duration metric received); header secret and VIN absent from logs and payloads while auth header is sent to the collector; unreachable collector and never-responding collector (200s, process alive, bounded shutdown); SIGTERM flush exits 0 with the span delivered; non-local plain-http endpoint leaves telemetry off with one warning and no connection; forced 500 via the fixture gives an error-status span while a 404 does not.

Test-only entry, not matched by the src/**/*.test.ts glob and not imported by production code. Builds buildApp with an in-memory WarehouseDb, makes listVehicles throw when FIXTURE_FAIL_LIST=1, listens on 127.0.0.1:PORT, prints 'warehouse-server on', and flushes telemetry on SIGTERM via shutdownTelemetry.

New README (none exists in the server folder). Covers run commands and a Telemetry section: off by default, enabled by an OTLP endpoint variable, list of supported OTEL_* variables, HTTPS rule for non-local endpoints, headers from environment only and never logged, what is and is not recorded (no bodies, VINs or DB spans), why the SDK is preloaded and not imported from index.ts, and a local collector example bound to loopback using OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT=http://127.0.0.1:4318 with placeholders only and any container image taken from registry.redhat.io.
No change expected: .env is already ignored on line 4. Only touched if a sample env file is added, which must hold placeholders only and keep a tracked name such as .env.example.

interfaces.name: TelemetryConfig
interfaces.signature: type TelemetryConfig = { enabled: true; serviceName: string } | { enabled: false; reason?: string }
interfaces.notes: reason never contains the endpoint URL, userinfo or header values.

interfaces.name: TelemetryOverrides
interfaces.signature: interface TelemetryOverrides { spanProcessors?: SpanProcessor[]; traceExporter?: SpanExporter; metricReader?: MetricReader }
interfaces.notes: Test seam for in-memory exporters. Property names follow the installed @opentelemetry/sdk-node version (metricReader vs metricReaders).

interfaces.name: resolveTelemetryConfig
interfaces.notes: Pure. Disabled unless an OTLP endpoint var is set, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED is not true, and every endpoint is https or loopback http. Fails closed.

interfaces.name: initTelemetry
interfaces.signature: function initTelemetry(env?: NodeJS.ProcessEnv, overrides?: TelemetryOverrides): TelemetryHandle | undefined
interfaces.notes: Idempotent. Returns undefined when disabled or when SDK start fails. Must run before fastify and node:http are imported.

interfaces.name: shutdownTelemetry
interfaces.notes: Default timeout 5000 ms. No-op when not started. Never rejects.

data_changes: New optional standard OpenTelemetry environment variables: OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TRACES_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_METRICS_ENDPOINT, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_HEADERS, OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_TIMEOUT, OTEL_SERVICE_NAME, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER, OTEL_TRACES_SAMPLER_ARG, OTEL_SDK_DISABLED, OTEL_METRIC_EXPORT_INTERVAL, OTEL_BSP_SCHEDULE_DELAY. No committed defaults except service.name 'warehouse-server'.
No feature flag beyond the endpoint variable: telemetry is off when it is unset.
tools/warehouse-server/package.json dev and start scripts change; root package-lock.json is regenerated.

test_approach.what: Spawn the real server with no OTEL_* variables using the npm start command shape; GET /api/vehicles returns 200 and no telemetry output appears (telemetry.e2e.test.ts).

Spawn the real server against a loopback fake collector with http/json. Given a running server, when /api/vehicles is called, then a trace with method, route, status and service.name, plus an HTTP server duration metric, reach the collector.
Same harness: header secret value and VIN are absent from logs and collector payloads, and the auth header is sent to the collector.

Same harness: unreachable and never-responding collectors leave responses at 200, the process alive and shutdown within the bound; SIGTERM flushes a pending span and exits 0; a non-local plain-http endpoint leaves telemetry off with one warning and no connection attempt.

In-process buildApp with app.inject and in-memory span and metric exporters through initTelemetry overrides: span attributes and service.name, 404 not an error, no VIN/body/query in attributes, flush and metrics on shutdown.
Fixture server with a forced 500 produces an error-status span, and a 404 in the same run does not.
Default off: initTelemetry with an empty env returns undefined, emits nothing and shutdownTelemetry resolves.

resolveTelemetryConfig: disabled with no endpoint or OTEL_SDK_DISABLED, local http and https allowed, remote http and unparsable URLs rejected, reason text never contains the URL, service.name default and override.

Existing suites (app, conformance, db, validate) run unchanged; npm run typecheck and root npm run test:warehouse and typecheck pass with no new warnings; npm audit shows no high or critical findings for new packages.

rollout: 1) Install dependencies, regenerate root package-lock.json, run npm audit. 2) Add telemetry.ts, instrument.ts and the unit tests. 3) Wire package.json scripts and index.ts shutdown; verify preload ordering with the e2e test and resolve two uncertainties: tsx --import preload ordering and whether ESM loader hooks are needed for node:http. 4) Add in-process span tests and the fixture; apply the contingent app.ts change only if a 4xx span is marked ERROR. 5) Write the README. 6) Run npm run typecheck, npm run test:warehouse and npm test -w @warehouse/server. Backwards compatible: with no OTEL_* variables behaviour, ports and responses are unchanged; the only visible difference is that SIGINT/SIGTERM now close the app before exit. Existing tests use buildApp and never import instrument.ts, so they need no collector. Rollback is removing the preload from the two scripts.
open_questions: The high-level open questions remain unresolved; this plan keeps the stated assumptions: server only, OTLP over HTTP (JSON or protobuf via OTEL_EXPORTER_OTLP_PROTOCOL, gRPC not documented as supported), traces and metrics both included, no WarehouseDb spans.
Does @fastify/otel with registerOnInitialization true mark handled 4xx errors as ERROR? The component test decides, and the contingent app.ts change is the fallback.

Does the installed @opentelemetry/sdk-node start a metric reader automatically from env? If not, add an explicit PeriodicExportingMetricReader with an OTLP metric exporter inside initTelemetry only, keeping endpoint and headers env-driven.
